prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mathematics, physics and chemistry

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with knowledge of the relationships between the microstructure of metallic materials and their mechanical properties, as well as the relationships between the structure and the processing methods used, and between properties and in-service performance.
Provide knowledge regarding the main degradation mechanisms of metallic materials and some possible remedies.
Be able to perform calculation activities to evaluate diffusive processes.
Be able to read fundamental diagrams such as phase diagrams and CCT and TTT curves of steels.
Be able to quantitatively interpret the results of main mechanical tests, such as the uniaxial tensile test.
For ferrous alloys, be able to evaluate the most suitable material for a specific operating condition also based on the applicable technological processes.
Be able to make material choices during the design phase of a component.
Understand the fundamental principles of materials science and engineering.
Know the link between microstructure, heat treatments and mechanical properties.
Know the classification and designation system for steels and the most important non-ferrous alloys.
Calculate mechanical properties from uniaxial test results.
Estimate the fraction of micro-constituents of a steel from state and transformation diagrams.
Select materials and treatments based on design specifications.
Analyze the reliability of a material and the factors that can lead to failure.
Diagnose incorrect treatments and propose corrective solutions.
Appropriately use technical terminology of mechanical metallurgy to comprehensively present analysis or research results orally.
Develop an autonomous study method that allows for updating on innovative material and process solutions in the metallurgical sector.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to metallic materials: Crystalline structure of metallic materials. Defects in crystalline lattices. Diffusion mechanisms in metallic materials.
Mechanical Properties: Mechanical properties and their measurement. Behavior of metallic alloys under mechanical stresses. Mechanisms of strain relief and strengthening.
Degradation Mechanisms: Introduction to creep, fatigue, wear and corrosion phenomena.

Phase Diagrams and Phase Transformations: Simple phase diagrams (complete miscibility, eutectics, peritectics). Solidification of metals. Kinetics of solid-state transformations. Introduction to Aluminum alloys.

Iron Metallurgy: Fe-Cementite system. Isothermal and continuous cooling transformation diagrams. Hardenability of steels. Heat treatments and brief notes on thermochemical treatments. Main microstructures of steels and their visualization.
Classification of steels and stainless steels: Effect of alloying elements in iron. Brief notes on the classification of steels. Introduction to stainless steels and their classification.
Introduction to the science and engineering of metallic materials: general classification of materials and their properties; classification of metallic materials and their properties.
Mechanical tests: mechanical properties and their measurement; fundamentals of fracture.
Structure of metals and atomic diffusion: typical crystalline structures of metallic materials; defects in crystalline lattices; solidification of metals; diffusion mechanisms.
Mechanics of metals: strengthening mechanisms; evolution of atomic structure during a mechanical test; strain relief mechanisms; effect of temperature on mechanical properties.
Degradation mechanisms: brief notes on fatigue, creep, wear, and corrosion phenomena.
Simple phase diagrams and phase transitions: notes on thermodynamics of materials; complete miscibility and eutectic diagrams; notes on the kinetics of solid-state transformations.

Iron metallurgy: diagrams with intermediate compounds; iron-cementite diagram; notes on cast irons and their classification; microstructures of steels and their mechanical properties; transformation diagrams of steels; heat treatments and hardenability of steels.
Alloy steels and stainless steels: effect of alloying elements in iron; classification and designation of steels; classification and designation of stainless steels.

Complex phase diagrams and non-ferrous alloys: diagrams with intermediate solid solutions and classification of brasses; complex aluminum and titanium diagrams and classification and designation of their alloys.
assessment_rules: The assessment consists of a 2-hour written exam plus an oral exam. Access to the oral exam is granted after passing the written exam with a minimum score of 16/30 (for initials A-K) or 15/30 (for initials L-Z). The final grade is obtained as the average of the two tests and must be above 18/30 (rounded up). For current students, optional and liberating intermediate tests are provided for both exams.
